checks: Fiberwise rearrangement optimizes the first moment at fixed allocated lengths by integrating height minus fill threshold against the signed density difference. Every box allocation is feasible, strict concavity gives unique optimal mass vectors, and mixtures fill the interval of moments. Convexity places every balanced centroid in the actual j-fiber.

The path intervals nest by rescaling densities to smaller mass. The two own-fiber fills squeeze their endpoints to l_j and u_j at zero. Compactness yields upper continuity of the value, and interpolation toward a feasible mass on the corresponding side yields lower continuity, including one-sided domain endpoints.

The feasible tangent cone consists of zero-total, zero-base-moment directions and the active bound signs. Its polar supplies finite multipliers even if the equality rows are dependent. Empty and full residuals have the correct signs, and the exact objective difference establishes sufficiency.

At two or more distinct free sites, the two-by-two normal system has determinant S ZZ−Z²>0 and ZZ>0. The objective derivative is b since varying masses have derivative of total one and derivative of centered base moment zero; the stated second derivative follows. A sole free anchor gives b'=−1 and projection of the residual conditions onto t is affine. A sole free off-anchor site or no free sites contributes a single mass.

Finite patterns yield continuous finite piecewise quadratics. The lower physical threshold is −b_V and the upper is b_U, so the integral has the stated sign and needs no derivative assertion at transition times. At rational data every admissible breakpoint is rational and each rational-linear-fractional path piece has only endpoint and square-root candidates for extrema.

The cap computation includes both oblique sides with a null common boundary, all slope knots and constant tails, and pure-base caps with the entire central interval. The two oriented minima are monotone in opposite directions. Thus the rational superlevel is a closed rational interval or empty; the range computation correctly excludes a height achieved only as t tends to zero.
